Text:
# BRAIN ABSCESS WITH NOCARDIA SPP.

Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) should be obtained in all patients with suspected brain abscess for diagnosis and determining number of lesions. Prior to beginning antimicrobial therapy, when possible, computed topographic (CT) - guided aspiration or surgery should be performed to obtain abscess material for determination of infectious pathogen.

Nocardia brain abscesses typically occur in immunocompromised patients and is often concomitant with disseminated or pulmonary infection. May occur with meningitis and/or ventriculitis.

# Consult Neurosurgery, Neurology, and Infectious Disease

# Duration of Therapy

Treat with IV therapy for total duration of 3-6 weeks in immunocompetent and 6 weeks in immunocompromised patients. Switch to oral antimicrobials after completing IV therapy and treat for an additional 3 months or more (longer for meningitis, immunocompromise or extensive disease).

---

References:

- Brouwer et al. N Engl J Med, 2014, 371(5)447-56
- Mandell chapter: Brain Abscess
- Sanford keyword: Brain Abscess
- Up-to-Date article: Treatment of Nocardiosis
Therapy:
## Initial IV Therapy

Sulfamethoxazole 75 mg/kg - trimethoprim 15 mg/kg IV q8h ($$$) R,DI <AND>
imipenem 1000 mg IV q8h ($$) [R]

If Nocardia isolate is susceptible to third generation cephalosporins:
Sulfamethoxazole 75 mg/kg - trimethoprim 15 mg/kg IV q8h ($$$) R,DI <AND>
ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h ($) [M]

If multiorgan or rapidly progressive disease, in addition to above therapy:
< ADD > Amikacin 7.5 mg/kg IV q12h ($$)

Alternative:
Linezolid 600 mg IV q12h ($$$$) DI,O < AND > imipenem 1 gm IV q8h ($$) R

## Oral Therapy, After Completing IV Therapy Above

For immunocompetent patients, treat with one of the below PO antimicrobials for at least 3 months after initial IV treatment. For immunocompromised patients, Treat with 2 of the below antimicrobials for at least one year.

Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim 2 DS PO q12h ($) R,DI

< OR >
Minocycline 100mg q12h($) DI

< OR >
Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875-125 mg PO q12h ($) R
Inpt: ORZID2 GMENU BRN ABSC NOCARDIA SPP
